subject: toilet paper
title: What If One Joke Emptied a Country's Shelves? In 1973 It Was Toilet Paper

scenes.text: What if one joke emptied a country's shelves? In 1973 it did, and nothing was running out.
December 11, 1973. A Wisconsin congressman warns the United States may face a toilet paper shortage within months.
December 19. Johnny Carson tells about twenty million viewers there's an acute shortage of toilet paper. It's a punchline.
Almost at once, shoppers fill their carts. Stores limit people to two or four rolls. Some lift the price from 39 cents to 69 to slow the buying.
The factories never slowed. TV news shows rolls coming off the line. It doesn't help. An empty shelf is its own proof.
Weeks later Carson tells viewers there is no shortage. The rush had made the only one there ever was.

description:
What if one joke emptied a country's shelves? In December 1973 it happened with toilet paper.
After Wisconsin congressman Harold Froehlich warned on 11 December of a possible shortage, Johnny Carson joked about it on the Tonight Show on 19 December in front of roughly 20 million viewers. Shoppers stripped the shelves, stores rationed rolls, and the buying created the very shortage people feared, even though production had not dropped. Carson later told viewers there was no shortage.

first_comment: Carson said he didn't want to be remembered as the man who created a false toilet paper scare. What's the strangest thing you've seen people panic-buy?
